subject.title: [Feature]: Discord: Re-process edited user messages (MESSAGE_UPDATE event)

question: Should Discord edited-message reprocessing land through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92091 with default-on edit/delete behavior, or should maintainers require disabled-by-default edit-only config before merge?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but choosing default-on behavior versus a new opt-in config surface changes existing Discord operator semantics and needs maintainer product intent.

options.title: Settle semantics in the linked PR
options.body: Use the open Discord edit/delete PR or a narrow replacement as the decision point, requiring live Discord proof and explicit default/config behavior before merge.

options.title: Require opt-in edit-only config
options.body: Implement handleEdits and edit debounce as disabled-by-default Discord config, matching this issue's compatibility proposal while adding config surface.

options.title: Split delete-to-cancel
options.body: Land edit-to-reprocess separately and keep delete-to-cancel on the broader lifecycle tracker if cancellation semantics are not ready.

recommendation.title: Settle semantics in the linked PR
recommendation.body: Use the open Discord edit/delete PR or a narrow replacement as the decision point, requiring live Discord proof and explicit default/config behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest prior review context and recent history across the Discord listener, startup, handler, and semantics surfaces involved here.
